metadata.title: The Singular LeBrun Transform: Complex Conformal and Contact Geometry
metadata.abstract: A holomorphic conformal structure is rigid in the presence of rational curves: a complex conformal manifold that is not conformally flat contains no immersed rational null geodesic. So a natural compactification of such a manifold, on which its null geodesics close up, must degenerate along the boundary. We study this phenomenon for the complex conformal manifold that LeBrun attached to a complex contact manifold $Z$ in inverting Salamon's twistor construction: the space $M_{\mathbb{C}}$ of balanced conics of $Z$ transverse to the contact distribution, with its holomorphic Riemannian metric of holonomy contained in $\mathrm{Sp}(n,\mathbb{C})\mathrm{Sp}(1,\mathbb{C})$. Its compactification by the degenerate conics of $Z$ forces the metric to become singular at the boundary. We develop a framework, the singular LeBrun transform, in which these singularities are a source of information rather than an obstacle: the singularities of the metric and of its curvature are read off from the degenerate rational curves of $Z$, locally through the contact neighbourhood of a curve and globally through the incidence variety. As an application, we give an alternative proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture that all positive quaternionic-Kähler manifolds are symmetric, which was recently claimed by OpenAI and by Hu, Liu and Wan. The emphasis of the paper, however, is less on this result than on the framework developed here, which should apply to other problems of the same kind; we conclude with two such directions, negative quaternionic-Kähler manifolds and a singular Merkulov transform for Legendre moduli spaces.
